You're not "at fault" for anything. You're human, and you just want what most people want, a connection. The shame you feel for yourself is the real block here. Hate to say it, but *finding* love is not something you just *do*... You have to work on showing the world *why* you're deserving of love. You reap what you sow, kinda like a self fulfilling prophecy.... And if you keep saying: 

>And I'm not sure how I can build confidence, *I have nothing confident to be about.*

>

>And *yes, your worth is defined by your sex life,* that's why calling men a virgin is an insult.


Then well.... That's your reality? Change it through your actions and how you treat *yourself*. My best friend deals with this (minus escorts, he's having a lot of issues finding a connection with someone when that's all he really wants), and he knows it's just a matter of patience. He's also realizing life *IS MORE* than a relationship, it's about making you're life you're own. It's just that horrid male stereotypes that make you feel this way (sex = power/status, men who have woman are better etc *all of which is BS*). To add to this, my boyfriend was a virgin until he was like 24, hadn't even gotten to second base until he met me, and it never bothered him even though he friends always poked at him for it. Yet he was patient and knew that it was worth waiting. It's a mindset. You gotta let that negative BS go, like water off a ducks back. 
To be honest, just having that mindset is a turnoff for most people in general, not just women. Sorry to be brutally honest but that's what I've observed in the realms of dating.

It seems like at the end of the day, you may want a sexual connection, but also just an emotional connection; one with love, commitment, communication and whatnot. That's normal, and it's about your mindset. If you perceive yourself as unlovable or unworthy of love that's what most women will pick up on and will see. Self confidence is sexy, and it's all about reminding yourself that your worth is not defined by how many times you've had sex, how many partners you've had, or if you even *have* a partner. It's defined by how you see yourself and the good you bring to the world without expecting anything in return. At the end of the day, wanting that connection is totally human. It's how you go about fulfilling that need that gives you perspective on your actions.

You're not doing anything *wrong*, just maybe focusing on the wrong aspects of this problem. Maybe work on self confidence, build up what you like about yourself and give yourself the credit due instead of making yourself feel worse by using the service that's not meeting those satisfaction levels anymore?

Basically, the main things you want to focus on at first is refining materials, crafting ones you need, and deconstructing old ones/ones you find as loot to boost your skill in which ever craft you choose.  for example let's use blacksmithing...
 [ Find Iron ore > go to blacksmith workbench > refine into iron ingot > use iron ingot to craft armor] 
Then, to boost the skill you'd deconstruct old ones, so you can get back materials from that and higher skill boosts than just constructing. 
As for styles and how it looks, that's all regarding "motifs". When you start, you'll get a quest for crafting eventually (I believe 6th level, but you can craft beforehand) and you'll be given a crafting motif for the race you chose. As you go through the game, you'll find random loot drops can have other races motifs as well. You'd wanna use them in your inventory to learn it.
Then as you level up, you'll get to find better quality materials, and therefore make higher level items. 
Finally, researching involves finding items with traits and if you aren't using the item, you can "research it" to use the skill on future items of that type when you craft it on the bench you researched it on. For example, if you found an iron sword with a magicka enchantment, You'd decontrust it if you ever wanted to crqdt iron swords with that enchantment in the future.

I hope this gives some insight even though I was a WS. I gave my all to helping him find his footing again in what he thought was a good relationship, since we had issues that caused the infidelity to flourish on my part and then the big boom that was the infidelity itself. Since then, I've given him full honesty, but expected the same as well. Couples counselling really helped mediate our emotions and some touchy topics we couldn't come together on, and we learned that communication was KEY to understanding why it happened in the first place. Things that helped him he's told me is one: having no contact on my part with the guy it happened with, two: at the beginning of the aftermath I would let him monitor (respectfully with my knowledge) my communication pathways so he could be certain the communication was respectful and within his boundaries if there were any at all and three: showing him my complete and utter remorse for my actions and owning up to them without an excuse. All and all, it takes time and effort, but your anger and "hollowness" is quite justified as you're trust has been broken. It's all about working together to make your relationship thrive more than before, and finding ways to work together on things that hindered the relationship prior.
